title: Attenuated cross-region shift with KV snapshot rollback for dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Summary: During a partial regional networking regression impacting inter-region routing, a subset of Dedicated tenants experienced elevated tail latency and transient KV cache desync. This ticket captures the attenuated shift strategy we executed to reduce blast radius, the emergency KV snapshot-and-rollback procedure we developed, and the follow-up mitigations for platform reliability. The goal was to preserve customer traffic by progressively shifting low-risk slices while enabling targeted remediation for tenants facing repeated KV misses. The document also includes communication templates and verification checks used to close the escalation.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-09 02:13 UTC - Automated health alerts triggered for region-us-east-2: elevated 95th pct latency and spike in 504s
2026-03-09 02:20 UTC - Oncall triage confirmed routing errors from regional gateway -> interconnect; early hypothesis: control-plane routing flap affecting KV affinity
2026-03-09 02:35 UTC - First customer report (enterprise tenant: FinOps Inc.) submitted via SRE escalation channel with degraded inference latency for Dedicated pool dp-ord-7
2026-03-09 02:50 UTC - Initiated attenuated shift: moved 10% of lowest-priority slices for affected pool to us-west-1 with traffic drain windows (30s buckets)
2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Observed drop in 95th pct for shifted slices; some tenants continued to show KV miss rate increase, correlated with prior writes from failed region
2026-03-09 03:18 UTC - Created emergency KV snapshot on surviving instances and staged a rollback image (kv-snap-20260309-0318) for impacted tenant shards
2026-03-09 03:32 UTC - Gradual rollout of snapshot rollback to 5% of affected shards; verification checks passed for 3/4 tenants before wider rollout
2026-03-09 04:10 UTC - Stabilized latency across Dedicated pool; communication sent to impacted customers with mitigation steps and ETA for root cause analysis
runbook_steps: Step 0 - Triage: Confirm scope in dashboards (per-tenant latency, 504s by region, KV miss rate). Capture graph snapshots and list of affected tenant IDs.

Step 1 - Attenuated shift plan: Identify non-critical slices (based on tenant priority and SLA tier). Create routing policy that shifts 10% contiguous slices to standby region using 'traffic-weight' override.
Step 2 - Safe drain: Enforce 30s drain windows and monitor inflight KV cache eviction metrics. If error rate increases >2x baseline, pause further shifts.

Step 3 - KV snapshot: On nodes with healthy KV view, take consistent snapshot (kv-snap-<ts>) and upload to internal S3 path. Tag affected shard IDs in snapshot metadata (manual tagging script: tools/kv/snapshot-tag.sh).

Step 4 - Rollback staging: Build rollback image with snapshot mount and start subject nodes in staging with canary traffic (5% of affected shards). Run smoke checks: token-level correctness, prefix cache hit rate, and 95th latency.
Step 5 - Canary verification: After 15m of stable metrics, progressively expand rollback to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m observation windows between steps.
Step 6 - Post-switch reconciliation: Trigger async KV repair jobs to rehydrate caches and reconcile write-ahead logs. Monitor for duplicate-write anomalies and stale-state warnings.

Step 7 - Customer comms: Use template in attachments to notify customers about mitigation, expected residual risk, and next steps. Offer technical RCA briefing and dedicated follow-up for high-touch tenants.
Step 8 - Close and capture artifacts: Record PRs, config changes, and dashboard snapshots. Kick off postmortem with blameless timeline and action owners (see postmortem_actions).

Emergency rollback: If rollback causes state divergence, pause and escalate to SRE lead, revert traffic overrides, and bring nodes back to pre-incident image while preserving logs for forensic analysis.
verification_checks: 95th and 99th latency back within 1.2x baseline for 30m
KV prefix hit rate recovered to >= 98% for affected shards
Error rate (5xx/4xx) within normal bounds and no new class of errors observed
No data-loss indicators on WAL replay; file-system integrity checks passed
Customer-specific smoke tests: identity model hash checks and sample prompt acceptance
customer_communication_snippets: Initial ack: "We acknowledge elevated latency impacting parts of your Dedicated capacity. Our current mitigation is an attenuated cross-region shift and targeted KV snapshot rollback for affected shards; engineers are monitoring closely. ETA for stabilization: ~3 hours."

Follow-up (post-mitigation): "We have stabilized traffic and applied a KV snapshot rollback to the affected shards. You may experience short-lived cache warmup; long-running requests are being retried gracefully. We will schedule an RCA within 48 hours."

High-touch offer: "For customers requiring deeper verification, we can run tenant-specific replay and provide a signed integrity report for your workloads. Please reply with a preferred contact and window."
postmortem_actions: Automate slice selection for attenuated shifts using priority + traffic profile rules (ENG-24600)
Add KV snapshot tooling to console UI with one-click snapshot-and-rollback for Dedicated pools
Improve observability: add per-tenant WAL lag metric and faster alerting thresholds
Run tabletop exercises quarterly for cross-region KV desync scenarios
Create a customer-facing runbook summary page and link in SLA docs
